thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated TLS handshake failure rate from frontend -> model-proxy in us-west-2 (5xx spike) :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Paging alice (oncall) and maya (sre)
alice (oncall): seeing the page, joining now. grabbing quick status from console.
jonah (eng): fwiw I just got an alert in the routing dashboards too — errors started ~ 2049991150ish.
alice (oncall): customer reports in Support saying slow/failed responses since ~ 2049991200. sean any threads?
sean (support): one customer (acct: big-retailer) reported 502s from inference endpoints at 2049991220. They saw TLS errors in their client logs.
maya (sre): adding initial hypothesis list inline: H1: cert rotation mismatch across Dedicated nodes H2: VPC peering path MTU causing TLS fragmentation and handshake drops H3: load balancer misconfig pushing old certs H4: transient routing flaps
eli (infra): noting recent cert-rotation job ran at 2049991100 across hosted control plane. I’ll check job logs.
jonah (eng): I'll tail model-proxy logs for handshake failures and client IPs.
alice (oncall): timeline so far:
- 2049991100 cert-rotation job kicked off (per eli)
- 2049991150 errors begin (dashboards)
- 2049991200 customer visible impact
- 2049991230 pager triggered
- 2049991240 oncall joined

eli (infra): cert-rotation job logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T10:05:02Z rotator: starting rotation for domain: api.redwood.internal
2026-03-15T10:06:12Z rotator: installed cert on control-plane-manager
2026-03-15T10:06:45Z rotator: queued worker nodes for rollout (region us-west-2)
2026-03-15T10:08:30Z rotator: completed push to kube secret on hostpool-1
2026-03-15T10:09:01Z rotator: ACK from kube-api but failed push to peered-vpc-nodes: timeout
```
eli (infra): see last line — push to peered VPC nodes timed out. digging into network logs now.
jonah (eng): model-proxy logs (relevant):
```
[2049991165] WARN tls: handshake error from 10.12.45.98: remote error: tls: handshake failure
[2049991166] WARN tls: handshake error from 10.12.45.111: read tcp 10.12.45.111:443->10.100.8.23:34567: i/o timeout
[2049991180] WARN tls: 3-way retransmit, resetting connection
```
maya (sre): that aligns with TLS handshake failure + timeouts. jonah can you `tcpdump` a failing flow and dump TLS ClientHello size?
jonah (eng): running quick tcpdump on node 10.12.45.111: `sudo tcpdump -n -s 1500 host 10.100.8.23 and port 443 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap`
jonah (eng): captured. initial analysis: many ClientHello packets being fragmented (seen as IP frag) and then no server response.
eli (infra): checking VPC peering link metrics — I see an unusual PMTU drop counter on the peering interface at 2049991158. MTU mismatch configuration change pushed in maintenance window earlier today?
alice (oncall): eli, can you confirm if any MTU changes were applied?
eli (infra): yes we pushed a change to align MTU to 1450 on peering route table at 2049991000 to address a prior jumbo frame issue. Looks like some nodes didn't pick it up.
maya (sre): that would cause fragmentation. TLS ClientHello with SNI + ALPN can exceed the smaller MTU and if DF flags set or fragmentation mishandled, handshake fails. Good hypothesis.
sean (support): customer observed `tls: handshake failure` in client logs and retried, sometimes worked after a few seconds.
jonah (eng): reproducer from inside peered node: `curl -v https://model-proxy.internal --resolve model-proxy.internal:443:10.12.45.111` yields:
```
* Connected to 10.12.45.111 (10.12.45.111) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: 
* SSL: error:140E0197:SSL routines:SSL_shutdown:protocol error
* Closing connection 0
```
jonah (eng): tcpdump shows ClientHello split into 2 fragments and server never sees assembled message.
eli (infra): network team: immediate mitigation options:
- revert MTU setting back to previous 9000 on the problematic VPC (fast, but may re-introduce earlier jumbo issues)
- enable MSS clamping on transit gateway to avoid fragmentation (likely non-disruptive)
- force rotator to re-run push with explicit retry/backoff for peered nodes (certs may not be installed)

alice (oncall): prioritize: MSS clamping first (lowest blast radius), then re-run cert push as a follow-up. who can apply MSS clamping?
eli (infra): I can apply MSS clamping on the transit-gw in ~5m. Scheduling now.
maya (sre): meanwhile I'll promote fallback: route traffic to fallback model-variant in us-east for high-risk customers via smart routing (reduces impact while infra change ongoing). jonah can you add routing rule?
jonah (eng): adding a canary route to reroute 10% traffic for the affected accounts: `POST /routing/overrides` payload applied.
jonah (eng): routing change applied at 2049991255. Observing backend error rate drop.
incident-bot: NOTE: Escalation to Eng-Infra requested by alice (oncall) at 2049991258
eli (infra): MSS clamping applied to transit-gw at 2049991260: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` equivalent on gateway.
jonah (eng): re-running curl test from peered client now...
jonah (eng): curl now completes TLS handshake successfully. `SSL connection using TLS1.3`
sean (support): customer reports services recovering. Thanks team.
maya (sre): monitoring for 10 minutes to ensure stability. If clean, we'll re-run rotator to ensure certs fully pushed.
eli (infra): rotator retry queued for 2049991280 with explicit retry to peered nodes.
alice (oncall): action items (assigned):
- eli: confirm rotator completed to peered nodes and post log (done by 2049991350)
- jonah: run a follow-up sweep of handshake error logs and collect pcap for one more flow (2049991300)
- maya: draft incident RCA outline covering cert rotator timeout + MTU mismatch and mitigation (2049991800)
- sean: follow up to customers with an incident update and mitigation steps (2049991400)

jonah (eng): follow-up pcap attached to thread (saved to /mnt/incident-artifacts/2049991234/handshake_after_clamp.pcap)
maya (sre): postmortem notes: preliminary root cause — combination of a partially-applied MTU change on the peering path causing fragmentation of ClientHello + a cert-rotation push that timed out for nodes behind that path. When fragments were dropped the TLS handshake couldn't complete, leading to client retries and 5xxs.
alice (oncall): are we comfortable resolving the page? any remaining customer impact?
sean (support): customers reporting intermittent 200s now, no new incidents. I'll keep open support tickets updated.
alice (oncall): closing page at 2049991268. We will keep thread open for RCA write-up and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
customer-success: thanks team — will update customers and internal comms once maya shares the RCA draft.
